prompt: A cathedral of stacked shipping containers around a light well.
spatialThesis: Containers stack into four walls around one vertical shaft; the shaft is the only daylight and it lands as a bright square on the floor at the centre.
visibleBeat: A container door in the wall swings open and the shaft light spills into the bay behind it.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a generic hall with a skylight
containers as flat boxes with the doors only painted on
a light well that is a light source with no shaft geometry around it

prompt: A spiral library where the stairs are the shelves.
spatialThesis: One continuous helix wraps a hollow core; every tread is deep enough to hold books, so the path up and the storage are the same surface.
visibleBeat: A book pulled from a tread leaves a gap you can see through into the core.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a staircase with separate bookcases standing next to it
a stack of flat rings that never connect into one climbable path

prompt: A bridge town: houses hanging under a single span over a dry canyon.
spatialThesis: One deck crosses the canyon and every dwelling hangs beneath it on rods, so the inhabited volume is under the walking surface, not on it.
visibleBeat: A hatch in the deck opens and a ladder drops into the house below it.
forbiddenSubstitutions: houses standing on top of the bridge
a canyon with water in it
houses floating with no visible connection to the deck

prompt: A brutalist observatory, one dome on three splayed legs, on a windswept plateau.
spatialThesis: A single heavy dome is lifted clear of the ground by three legs that splay outward, so the space beneath it is open and crossed by their shadows.
visibleBeat: The dome shutter slides open and the slot of sky it reveals tracks across the plateau floor.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a dome sitting directly on the ground
four legs or a solid pedestal instead of three splayed legs
a smooth glossy dome, which contradicts brutalist
mustName: that wind is rendered as motion of objects, not as simulated air

prompt: A flooded parking garage with ramps rising out of the water.
spatialThesis: Flat decks repeat at fixed intervals; the waterline cuts them horizontally so the lowest deck is submerged and the ramps are the only continuous path from wet to dry.
visibleBeat: Something floating drifts down the ramp until the waterline stops it.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a garage with a puddle instead of a waterline that cuts the geometry
ramps that do not connect two decks
water rendered as a flat coloured plane with no interaction

prompt: A watchtower made of one continuous ramp coiling around an empty core.
spatialThesis: There are no floors: a single ramp coils from ground to top around an empty vertical core, so every height is reachable and nothing is enclosed.
visibleBeat: An object dropped into the core falls past the ramp turns all the way to the ground.
forbiddenSubstitutions: stacked floors joined by stairs
a solid central column instead of an empty core
a ramp that does not actually reach the top

prompt: A forest where the trees are ribcages and the ground breathes.
spatialThesis: Paired curved ribs rise from a soft floor in place of trunks, so the canopy is a lattice of arcs and the sky is visible in slices between them.
visibleBeat: The ground rises and falls, and the ribs standing in it tilt with each breath.
forbiddenSubstitutions: normal trees with bone-coloured bark
ribs as decoration attached to a cylindrical trunk
a static floor with a scrolling texture standing in for breathing
mustName: that the ground is animated as a whole surface, not simulated soft tissue

prompt: A tidal cave with a colony of glowing anemones on the ceiling.
spatialThesis: The cave is wider than it is tall and the light comes from above: the anemone colony on the ceiling lights the water below it and leaves the walls dark.
visibleBeat: An anemone contracts when something passes under it and its light shrinks with it.
forbiddenSubstitutions: anemones on the floor
a lit cave with the anemones added as decoration
glow as an emissive texture with no light reaching the water

prompt: A giant fallen tree hollowed into a village.
spatialThesis: One horizontal trunk lies across the scene and the whole settlement is inside it, so the village is a tube: doors face outward along the bark, rooms line up along the axis.
visibleBeat: A door in the bark opens and light from inside the trunk falls onto the ground.
forbiddenSubstitutions: houses built on top of or beside the trunk
a standing tree
a trunk that is solid, with the village only implied

prompt: A coral reef growing over a sunken radio tower.
spatialThesis: A man-made lattice stands vertically and organic growth thickens it from the bottom up, so the silhouette is straight at the top and swollen at the base.
visibleBeat: A section of coral releases a cloud that drifts up the lattice.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a reef with no tower inside it
a clean tower with coral only on the seabed around it
coral as a texture on the tower rather than added volume

prompt: A field of slow-moving grazing rock creatures.
spatialThesis: An open plain with no vertical structure except the creatures themselves; they are spread out, so distance between them is the only thing that reads as depth.
visibleBeat: A creature lowers its head to the ground, then moves a body length to the next patch.
forbiddenSubstitutions: boulders that do not move
creatures that look organic rather than stone
a crowded herd, which destroys the emptiness the sentence asks for

prompt: A clock tower where the gears are big enough to walk on.
spatialThesis: The mechanism is the architecture: gears lie in parallel planes at different heights and the walkable surface is the teeth and spokes, so the route through the tower is the gear train.
visibleBeat: The large gear advances one tooth and everything standing on it moves with it.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a tower with a clock face and gears hidden inside
gears that spin but carry nothing
gears that are all the same size, which removes the train

prompt: A drawbridge worked by a counterweight full of water.
spatialThesis: Two masses hang on opposite sides of one pivot; the bridge deck is low when the counterweight is light and rises as the counterweight fills, so height encodes the state of the machine.
visibleBeat: The counterweight fills, drops, and the deck swings up out of the way.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a bridge that rises with no visible counterweight
a counterweight that never changes
a counterweight and a deck that are not connected across the pivot
mustName: that the water is a level inside the counterweight, not fluid simulation

prompt: A water-driven mill that lifts crates onto a platform.
spatialThesis: A single chain of transmission runs from low to high: wheel at the water, shaft across, lift at the platform, so the whole machine reads left to right and bottom to top.
visibleBeat: A crate rides the lift up and lands on the platform, and the wheel keeps turning.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a mill wheel that turns while the lift moves independently
crates that teleport to the platform
a lift with no visible drive from the wheel

prompt: An orrery the size of a room, planets on brass arms.
spatialThesis: Everything orbits one centre in the middle of the floor; the arms differ in length and height so the paths are concentric rings you can walk between.
visibleBeat: The arms sweep at different rates and two of them cross.
forbiddenSubstitutions: free-floating spheres with no arms
all arms the same length, which destroys the concentric reading
a wall-mounted model rather than a room-sized one

prompt: A pneumatic tube station that sorts capsules into three chutes.
spatialThesis: One trunk tube arrives and splits at a single junction into three chutes that fan out at different angles, so the branching point is the visual centre.
visibleBeat: A capsule arrives, the sorting head turns, and the capsule leaves down one of the three chutes.
forbiddenSubstitutions: three separate tubes with no shared junction
capsules that vanish at the junction
a sorting head that never moves

prompt: A lighthouse in fog so thick the beam is the only straight line.
spatialThesis: Everything except the tower is soft and near-formless; the beam is a hard-edged cone that cuts the fog and is the only element with a defined direction.
visibleBeat: The beam sweeps and briefly picks something out of the fog before losing it again.
forbiddenSubstitutions: clear air with a light on top of a tower
fog as a flat grey background instead of a volume the beam passes through
a beam that does not rotate
mustName: that fog is a rendered volume effect, not simulated scattering

prompt: Dawn over a frozen lake with steam coming off the cracks.
spatialThesis: A flat horizontal plane fills the ground and the only vertical elements are thin columns of steam rising from a network of cracks, so the cracks draw the composition.
visibleBeat: A crack widens and a new column of steam starts from it.
forbiddenSubstitutions: open water instead of ice
steam that rises everywhere rather than from the cracks
a night or midday sky, which loses the low dawn light

prompt: A sandstorm rolling into an abandoned drive-in cinema.
spatialThesis: A large flat screen stands at one end facing rows of empty ground, and the storm arrives as a wall from behind the screen, so depth is read by how much of the field is still visible.
visibleBeat: The sand front reaches the screen and the far rows disappear before the near ones.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a uniform dust haze with no advancing front
a screen with a picture on it, which contradicts abandoned
cars parked and intact, which contradicts abandoned
mustName: that the sand front is an animated volume, not simulated particulate flow

prompt: A tunnel lit only by the train that is about to arrive.
spatialThesis: A long straight tube with the only light source at one end and moving; the walls are revealed progressively as the light approaches, so the lit length is the clock.
visibleBeat: The headlight grows, the walls light up in sequence, and the train reaches the platform.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a lit tunnel with a train added
a stationary train
lighting that reveals the whole tunnel at once

prompt: A monsoon courtyard where the rain sheets off every roof edge.
spatialThesis: A closed square of low roofs around one open middle; water leaves along every eave, so the courtyard is framed by falling sheets on all four sides.
visibleBeat: A sheet breaks where a roof edge is damaged and the water lands in a different place.
forbiddenSubstitutions: rain falling uniformly from the sky with no roof edges involved
an open landscape instead of an enclosed courtyard
sheets that do not start at a roof edge
mustName: that rain is an animated effect, not fluid simulation

prompt: A space where gravity points toward the nearest wall.
spatialThesis: There is no single floor: every surface is walkable and objects rest against whichever surface is closest, so the same room reads differently depending on where you stand.
visibleBeat: An object crosses the midpoint between two walls and falls to the other one.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a normal room with objects glued to the walls
a single reoriented gravity direction for the whole space
objects that never move between surfaces

prompt: A room that is the inside of a sorting algorithm.
spatialThesis: Columns of different heights stand in a single row and the order of the row is the whole content of the space; movement happens along that row and nowhere else.
visibleBeat: Two columns are marked, they swap places, and the row is one step closer to sorted.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a room with a screen showing an algorithm
columns that move without any comparison being shown
a finished sorted row with no process visible
mustName: that the algorithm is one named sorting procedure, chosen and stated, not algorithms in general

prompt: A place built out of the negative space of a staircase.
spatialThesis: The solid is where a staircase is not: the treads and risers are voids cut out of a block, so the walkable surface is the underside of steps that do not exist.
visibleBeat: Light passes through the step voids and draws the missing staircase on the floor.
forbiddenSubstitutions: an ordinary staircase
a block with rectangular holes that do not form a stair profile
an inverted staircase, which is still a staircase

prompt: A landscape where distance is measured in silence.
spatialThesis: Density falls off with distance: objects crowd near the viewer and thin out to nothing, so how empty a region is says how far away it is.
visibleBeat: Moving forward brings a new object out of the empty region and the region beyond it empties further.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a uniformly populated landscape with fog for depth
an audio-only interpretation with no spatial consequence
a literal text label reading silence
mustName: that silence is expressed as visual density, since the system has no spatial audio

prompt: Make me a chess engine that beats me.
spatialThesis: The honest reading is a space about chess, not a chess program: a board-shaped floor with pieces standing on it as objects.
visibleBeat: A piece moves one square and stops on the new square.
forbiddenSubstitutions: claiming a working engine was produced
an empty room with nothing built, because a refusal must still produce a world
a rendered chessboard image instead of a space you are inside
mustName: that no chess engine and no legal-move search was produced
that the world is a spatial reading of the request, not the request itself

prompt: Write a haiku about the sea.
spatialThesis: The honest reading is a sea-shaped space: one horizontal water plane, one horizon, nothing else competing with it.
visibleBeat: A swell crosses the water plane from one edge to the other.
forbiddenSubstitutions: rendering three lines of text as the deliverable
an empty scene, because a refusal must still produce a world
a beach scene with buildings, which is not what the sentence names
mustName: that no poem was written and that text generation is not what this system does

prompt: Model a mechanical wristwatch, exploded view, every component labelled.
spatialThesis: The honest reading is a room-sized arrangement of separated parts along one axis, which is a space; the labelled engineering drawing is not.
visibleBeat: The components slide apart along the axis and stop at their spread positions.
forbiddenSubstitutions: a labelled 2D diagram
a closed watch with no separation, which drops the exploded reading
per-component text labels presented as if they were verified part names
mustName: that no component names are asserted, because the system has no watch parts list
that this is product visualisation, outside real-time generative environments

prompt: Recreate my apartment from this floor plan: three rooms, sixty square metres, balcony to the south.
spatialThesis: The honest reading is three connected volumes with one opening on one side; the numbers are honoured as proportions, not as a surveyed reconstruction.
visibleBeat: A door between two of the rooms opens and you can see from one into the other.
forbiddenSubstitutions: claiming the result matches a real floor plan
one open volume instead of three rooms
a balcony on the wrong side or missing entirely
mustName: that no floor plan was received and the layout is invented from the numbers
that square metres are treated as proportion, not as a measured area

prompt: Simulate an epidemic across ten thousand people and plot the curve.
spatialThesis: The honest reading is a crowd-shaped space at a scale the browser can hold: many small bodies spread over a plane, with state visible as their appearance.
visibleBeat: A body changes state and the bodies next to it change soon after.
forbiddenSubstitutions: drawing a chart as the deliverable
claiming ten thousand agents when fewer are built
an empty scene, because a refusal must still produce a world
mustName: that the population is reduced to what the frame budget allows, with the number stated
that no epidemiological model is claimed and no curve is plotted
